title: 25 prompts your team will actually use
sub: One for every job that eats a Tuesday. Written for UK teams, in plain words, for whichever assistant you already pay for.

cards.title: Catch up on a long email thread
cards.body: What is being decided, who is waiting on whom, and the one thing you have to do.

cards.title: Turn a meeting into who does what
cards.body: Owners, actions and dates, in a table. Anything with no owner gets marked.

cards.title: A first draft from your notes
cards.body: Your template, your notes, and honest [GAP] marks where the notes fall short.

cards.title: Read a long document properly
cards.body: The ten questions to ask before agreeing, each with the clause it comes from.

cards.title: Rewrite for someone with five minutes
cards.body: Every fact kept, the padding gone, and a list of what was cut.

cards.title: Prepare for a difficult conversation
cards.body: Three points in order, two likely objections, and one opening sentence.

cards.title: Every requirement in a tender
cards.body: All of them in a table, in the buyer's words, including the one on page 38.

cards.title: A proposal from the first call
cards.body: Written in the client's own language, not your standard paragraphs.

cards.title: Why you lose deals
cards.body: Your own lost-deal notes grouped into the objections that keep coming back.

cards.title: A brief into a four-week plan
cards.body: Channels, formats and owners, built only from what the brief actually says.

cards.title: Check a draft against your style
cards.body: One voice across the team without someone editing every piece by hand.

cards.title: Case study interview questions
cards.body: Questions that get numbers and specifics rather than polite compliments.

cards.title: The weekly client update
cards.body: What moved, what is blocked, what you need from them. Under 200 words.

cards.title: Reply to a complaint properly
cards.body: Owns the problem, explains, commits. No grovelling and no deflecting.

cards.title: Hand a client to a colleague
cards.body: The full handover, pulled from the files and threads that already exist.

cards.title: Explain the numbers that moved
cards.body: Board-ready commentary on the variances that clear your own threshold.

cards.title: A spreadsheet someone else built
cards.body: Inputs, calculations, totals, and every place it quietly does not add up.

cards.title: Two quotes, compared on small print
cards.body: Terms, exclusions, uplifts, notice and exit costs, side by side, clause by clause.

cards.title: Write the process down
cards.body: One written procedure from three colleagues' different versions of the same job.

cards.title: Explain what went wrong
cards.body: Timeline, impact and actions from a messy chat log. No blame attached.

cards.title: A job description for the real role
cards.body: Built from what the person actually does all week, in plain inclusive language.

cards.title: A first month for a new starter
cards.body: Week by week, shaped by the role and the team they are joining.

cards.title: Test a board paper first
cards.body: The eight questions a sceptical non-executive will ask, in the order they ask them.

cards.title: A ninety-day plan for one team
cards.body: Who, which tool, what to build and what to measure. One page.

cards.title: A strategy people can repeat
cards.body: Six hundred words anyone can read in five minutes and say back in a meeting.
